Class MKScreen

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.AbstractContainerEventHandler
net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.MKScreen
All Implemented Interfaces:
net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.ContainerEventHandler, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.events.GuiEventListener, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.Renderable, net.minecraft.client.gui.components.TabOrderedElement
public class MKScreen extends net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen
Base class for standalone screens built with MenuKit: full-screen, client-local, interactive UIs not tied to a container menu.

Extends vanilla's Screen directly; a MenuKit standalone screen is a vanilla Screen, so ecosystem mixins into Screen affect it identically.

Its panels live in one host

The screen's panels go into a standalone PanelHost (§0065), attached to ScreenPanelRegistry so global questions (what claims a point, is a modal up) see them alongside anything injected onto this screen. The host places each panel by its PanelPosition:
  • main(): the screen's frame, centred (one per screen);
  • region(OutsideRegion): around the main panel;
  • screenAnchor(InsideRegion): screen chrome (a back button, a title);
  • center(): an overlay, drawn on top (dialogs);
  • pixel(...): exact coordinates.
An unplaced panel takes the standalone default (PanelPosition.standaloneDefaults(List)): the first becomes main(), later ones stack below it. A region(...) panel with no main to anchor to is rejected at construction.

Render follows the one LayerPlan (FLOW, dim, OVERLAY), composed by the registry with any injected hosts on this screen. Input: the screen routes its own panels (topmost first, modal-aware), then vanilla widgets, then eats a click its panels claim.

See Also:
  • for panels on vanilla screens

    • PANEL_PADDING

      protected static final int PANEL_PADDING
      Padding inside each styled panel (pixels from panel edge to content). The padding applied is style-conditional via Panel.interiorPadding(): this value for styled panels, 0 for PanelStyle.NONE.

  • Method Details

    • hideTitle

      protected final void hideTitle()
      No title band: the title is not drawn and no room is kept for it, so the main panel can reach the top of the screen. The title still names the screen for narration. Call from the subclass constructor.
